name: ScreenConnect Process Started
description: Searches for instances of the ScreenConnect remote-access software starting. Collin County does not allow any remote-access clients aside from Bomgar.
note:
# ScreenConnect Process Start — Investigation Guide
### Disclaimer
> This investigation guide was created using generative AI technology and has been reviewed to improve its accuracy and relevance. While every effort has been made to ensure its quality, we recommend validating the content and adapting it to suit your specific environment and operational needs.

# 1. Validate the Process

Review the process event and confirm:

Process name and path
Expected ScreenConnect/ConnectWise Control installation path?
Is the executable running from a user-writable or temporary directory?
File hash
Compare against known-good ScreenConnect binaries.
Check whether the hash is associated with the expected version.
Digital signature
Confirm the executable is signed by the expected vendor.
Investigate unsigned or invalidly signed binaries.
Process command line
Look for unusual arguments, encoded commands, scripts, or suspicious child-process behavior.

# 2. Identify the Execution Context

Determine:

Which user started the process?
Was it running as SYSTEM, a local administrator, or a standard user?
Was the process started interactively or by a service?
Is the host expected to have ScreenConnect installed?

A ScreenConnect process starting on a system where the software is not expected may indicate unauthorized remote access software or a potentially compromised endpoint.

# 3. Review Parent and Child Processes

Investigate the process tree.

Potentially suspicious parent processes:

powershell.exe
cmd.exe
wscript.exe / cscript.exe
mshta.exe
Office applications
Web browsers
Archive utilities
Unknown or unsigned executables

Review child processes for:

Command shells
PowerShell
Credential dumping tools
Discovery commands
File staging or compression
Other remote access tools

# 4. Investigate Network Activity

Review network connections associated with the process:

Destination IPs and domains
Connection timing relative to the alert
Whether the connection is to expected ScreenConnect infrastructure
Unusual external destinations
Connections to internal systems unrelated to remote support

Pay particular attention to a ScreenConnect process that establishes network connections shortly after being launched by a suspicious process or from an unusual location.

# 5. Establish the Business Context

## Determine:

Is ScreenConnect approved for this host?
Is the device managed by an authorized IT/support team?
Was there an active support session or maintenance activity?
Was the software recently installed or updated?
Is the initiating user authorized to use remote support software?

# Check for related events such as:

Software installation
New service creation
File creation
Scheduled task creation
User logon
Remote logon
Other security alerts
6. Determine Disposition

## Likely Benign

Known-good signed binary
Expected installation path
Approved ScreenConnect deployment
Authorized user or support activity
Normal network connections

## Requires Further Investigation

Unexpected host or user
Unusual installation path
Unsigned or modified executable
Suspicious parent process
Unexpected child processes
Unusual network activity

## Potentially Malicious

ScreenConnect was downloaded or executed by a suspicious process
Binary is renamed, unsigned, or running from a temporary/user-writable directory
Evidence of unauthorized remote access
Suspicious post-execution activity or lateral movement
query: process.name : ("ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe" or "ScreenConnect.WindowsClient.exe" or "ScreenConnect.WindowsBackstageShell.exe" or "ScreenConnect.WindowsFileManager.exe") and event.type : "start"
